motionDesigner.title: Motion design intern

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.subtitle: The rules everyone agrees to by using Inturn.

sections.heading: Who we are
sections.body: Inturn is operated by We Make It Grow, a company registered in Tunis, Tunisia. By creating an account on inturn.tn you accept these Terms of Service together with our Privacy Policy and Cookie Policy.

sections.heading: Who can use Inturn
sections.body: Inturn is for: (a) students aged 18+ enrolled in a recognised institution, (b) companies or non-profits offering legitimate internships, and (c) administrators authorised by Inturn. Accounts found to be impersonating others, scraping data, or operating bots will be suspended.

sections.heading: Internship listings
sections.body: Companies are responsible for the accuracy and legality of every internship they publish. Inturn reviews listings before they go live, but does not guarantee the quality, safety, or legality of any third-party listing. Interns are responsible for performing their own due diligence before applying.

sections.heading: Compensation and contracts
sections.body: Inturn facilitates introductions only. Any internship contract, payment, or compensation is a direct relationship between the intern, the host company, and (where applicable) the university. Inturn is not a party to that contract and is not liable for non-payment, scope changes, or termination by either side.

sections.heading: Acceptable use
sections.body: Don't post harmful, illegal, harassing, fraudulent, or sexually explicit content. Don't try to compromise the platform, bypass rate limits, or send unsolicited bulk messages. Don't impersonate someone else, including Inturn staff. Don't ask interns to pay you for an internship.

sections.heading: Intellectual property
sections.body: You keep the IP rights to content you upload (CVs, project descriptions, deliverables). You grant Inturn a worldwide, non-exclusive licence to display, store, and back up that content as needed to run the service. Inturn's branding, code, and design are © We Make It Grow.

sections.heading: Suspension and termination
sections.body: We can suspend or close any account that violates these Terms, with or without notice depending on severity. You can close your own account at any time from the account settings — your data is then deleted within 30 days, except where legal record-keeping obligations require us to retain specific items longer.

sections.heading: Liability
sections.body: Inturn is provided 'as is.' To the extent permitted by Tunisian law, our maximum liability for any claim arising from the use of the platform is limited to the fees you paid us in the 12 months before the claim arose (€0 for free accounts).

sections.heading: Governing law
sections.body: These Terms are governed by the laws of Tunisia. Disputes will be resolved by the competent courts of Tunis unless a mandatory consumer-protection forum applies for your country of residence.

sections.heading: Changes to these Terms
sections.body: We may update these Terms. Material changes are announced by email and on the platform at least 14 days before they take effect. Continued use of Inturn after that means you accept the updated Terms.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.subtitle: What we collect, why, and what you can do about it.

sections.heading: Data controller
sections.body: The controller of your personal data is We Make It Grow (the operator of Inturn), Tunis, Tunisia. You can reach the data protection contact at privacy@inturn.tn.

sections.heading: What we collect
sections.body: Account data (email, name, role) from Clerk; profile data you enter (university, skills, CV, portfolio links); usage data (pages viewed, actions taken — used to keep the platform secure and to fix bugs); content you create (applications, comments, deliverables). We do not knowingly collect data from anyone under 18.

sections.heading: Why we use it
sections.body: To create your account and authenticate you (Clerk); to show your profile to companies you apply to; to send transactional emails (welcome, application updates, deadlines); to keep the platform secure (rate-limit + fraud detection); to fix bugs and improve the product. We do not sell personal data and we do not run targeted advertising.

sections.heading: Legal basis
sections.body: We process personal data under the legal basis of (a) contract — running the service you signed up for; (b) legitimate interest — keeping the platform secure and improving it; and (c) consent — for optional cookies and any marketing emails (you can withdraw at any time).

sections.heading: Sub-processors
sections.body: We share data with: Clerk (authentication), Neon (database hosting, EU region), Vercel (web hosting, EU region), Resend (transactional email), Anthropic (AI-assisted features — only the text you submit for that specific request). All sub-processors are bound by data-processing agreements.

sections.heading: Retention
sections.body: Active accounts: as long as you're using the service. Closed accounts: deleted within 30 days, except (a) audit logs we are legally required to retain, and (b) end-of-internship records — these are signed artefacts; we keep them until you ask for deletion.

sections.heading: Your rights
sections.body: You have the right to access, correct, export, or delete your personal data. Email privacy@inturn.tn from the address on file. We respond within 30 days. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with the Tunisian Instance Nationale de Protection des Données Personnelles (INPDP) or your local supervisory authority.

sections.heading: International transfers
sections.body: Our hosting and sub-processors operate from the EU and Tunisia. Where data is transferred outside the EU, we rely on Standard Contractual Clauses and equivalent safeguards.

sections.heading: Security
sections.body: We use TLS in transit, encrypted storage at rest, rate-limiting against abuse, and least-privilege access controls. No system is perfectly secure — please report vulnerabilities to security@inturn.tn.

cookies.title: Cookie Policy
cookies.subtitle: The cookies we set and what they do.

sections.heading: Essential cookies
sections.body: These are required for Inturn to work. We use: __clerk_* (authentication, set by Clerk); inturn-theme (your light/dark preference); inturn-cookie-consent (records your choice on this banner — so we don't keep asking). You cannot disable essential cookies and continue to use the service.

sections.heading: Optional cookies
sections.body: We currently do not set analytics or marketing cookies. If we do in the future (e.g. anonymous product analytics), they will only load after you explicitly accept the cookie banner. You can change your choice any time by clearing the inturn-cookie-consent value in your browser storage.

sections.heading: Third-party cookies
sections.body: Clerk (our authentication provider) sets its own cookies under its own privacy policy: https://clerk.com/privacy. When you embed a meeting link or watch a video, that third party may set its own cookies under its own policy.

meta.title: Inturn — Real internships. Not coffee runs.
meta.description: Inturn is the internship platform for Tunisia. Companies post real projects, students do real work, everyone gets a verifiable record of what shipped.

hero.companyDeck: Inturn turns internships into actual projects. You scope the work, we structure it. Students ship real outputs — audits, code, designs, research — in a workspace built for the loop. Everyone walks away with a record of what got done.
hero.internDeck: Inturn matches you to projects companies have actually scoped. You get a workspace with a brief, tasks, weekly check-ins, and a verifiable certificate at the end that links to what you shipped. No photocopies. No watching from a desk.
hero.tickerRest: running this week · Tunis, Sfax, Sousse, Remote

problem.title: From scattered to structured.
problem.subtitle: The work doesn’t change — the system around it does. That’s the whole difference between an intern you forget and one whose output you can point to.

solution.deck: Inturn is opinionated software. Companies post a project — not a vague role — with deliverables defined upfront. Each intern gets a workspace with tasks, a weekly check-in, a deliverables tab that versions every submission forever, and a supervisor who can't disappear because the dashboard tells them they have two reviews waiting.
solution.caption: Every version. Every comment. Every approval. Kept forever.

pillars.title: Three things old internships get wrong. We fix all three.
pillars.card1Body: You post a project, not a vague "design intern" role. Deliverables defined upfront — three to ten outcomes. We won't let you publish without them. If you can't list five, you don't need an intern, you need a hire.
pillars.card2Body: The supervisor dashboard surfaces what's waiting on them every time they open Inturn. Reviews older than 48 hours get flagged. Weekly check-ins are pre-scheduled. The system makes mentorship the path of least resistance.
pillars.card3Body: Every certificate links to the actual deliverables submitted, the tasks completed, the supervisor's rating. Verifiable at inturn.app/v/'{id}'. Employers see what shipped, not what was promised.

virtual.deck: A virtual internship on Inturn is the full workspace, built to work remotely — async task templates, weekly check-ins, versioned deliverables. Tunis runs on European time, so a day with a team in Tunis, Paris or Berlin lines up by default.
virtual.bullet1: Structure beats distance — every task has scope, output, deadline.
virtual.bullet2: Work beyond your city — even for EU and remote-first teams.
virtual.bullet3: Hybrid by default, virtual opt-in — low-risk to try.

mission.title: More than internships. A step toward something bigger.
mission.deck: Inturn isn't just fixing a broken process — it's building toward a better future. We align with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, so every internship run through the platform creates real impact for students, companies, and society.
mission.sdg1Body: Structured, mentored internships that strengthen the education-to-work transition — turning what students learn into real-world skill.
mission.sdg2Body: Better pathways into youth employment, and a way for SMEs to grow by tapping affordable, genuinely skilled early talent.
mission.sdg3Body: Open doors for every student — including women and underrepresented groups who too often struggle to access meaningful internships.
mission.sdg4Body: We collaborate with universities, NGOs and companies to build a strong internship ecosystem in Tunisia — and beyond.
mission.footLead: With Inturn, every internship is a step toward

meta.title: How it works — Inturn
meta.description: The full Inturn flow, from posting a project to issuing the certificate. Seven steps. Eight weeks. Real work.

hero.titleLead: The full loop — from blank page to
hero.deck: No screenshots in a deck. No "schedule a demo" wall. Here's literally every step. From the supervisor's side, the intern's side, and what the system does in between.

steps.step1Title: Describe the project. AI does the rest.
steps.step1Body: Paste a paragraph: "We want to refresh our brand over 12 weeks with two interns — one for visual, one for research." Inturn drafts your goals (max 3), phases, deliverables (3–10), and skill list. You edit anything you don't agree with. There's a manual form if you'd rather skip the AI — same data model, different door.
steps.step1OutputsValue: Goals · Phases · Deliverables · Skills · Pay range
steps.step2Title: Publish — and the project flips from Draft to Active.
steps.step2Body: You add the role title, scope, slots, supervisor, pay. Two application questions max — anything more and applicants drop off. Pick "public marketplace" or "private link only" if you're hiring someone you already know. Publishing creates the marketplace listing and activates the project.
steps.step2SeeValue: live preview of the marketplace card on the right of the form
steps.step3Body: Students browsing Inturn see your role ranked by match score against their profile — skills, location, goals. The match band at the top reads "Here are 7 internships matched to you." Your listing shows up with the actual pay number, the actual deliverables, and the actual supervisor — no surprises.
steps.step4Title: Review applications in one place. Accept in one click.
steps.step4Body: Each application is the student's profile + their answers to your two questions + a portfolio link. You review, you shortlist, you accept. Inturn doesn't run interviews for you — it makes them shorter. When you accept, the intern's workspace spins up automatically with the brief already loaded.
steps.step4HappensValue: Workspace created · brief copied · Jitsi link generated · first weekly check-in scheduled
steps.step5Title: Day one is already set up.
steps.step5Body: The intern lands in their workspace. Brief at the top. Tasks pre-populated from the deliverables. Calendar showing the weekly check-ins. Activity feed empty (for now). They don't need to ask "what do I do today" — the system answered before they showed up.
steps.step6Title: The loop runs itself. You tip in where it matters.
steps.step6Body: Intern moves tasks across the board. Submits deliverables as v1, then v2 with notes. Supervisor reviews — either approves or requests changes. Comments thread on every artifact. Every Friday at 14:00, the weekly check-in happens with a pre-built agenda. Nothing falls through.
steps.step6FrictionValue: "Needs review" can't be ignored — flagged after 48h
steps.step7Title: The certificate is generated the moment the last deliverable is approved.
steps.step7BodyLead: Project complete. The supervisor's final rating is in. Inturn generates the certificate automatically — signed by the supervisor, signed by the platform, signed by the intern. The verification link goes live at
steps.step7BodyTail: — anyone can hit it, see what shipped, see the supervisor's name, verify the dates. The intern shares it. The next employer trusts it.
steps.step7ShipsValue: PDF · public link · LinkedIn share · QR code

limits.deck: We're a workspace, not a recruiter. Knowing what we're not is what lets us be good at what we are.
limits.card1Body: No 6-step interview flow, no take-home assignments, no algorithmic ranking pretending to be smart. You review the application, you talk to the candidate however you want, you accept inside Inturn.
limits.card2Body: Companies handle payroll their normal way. Inturn shows the pay number, the intern verifies it before accepting, and we send reminders if the payment date slips. The money flow stays where it is.
limits.card3Body: If you don't have someone willing to commit 30 minutes a day to a junior person, Inturn can't fix that. The product is built for teams who want to mentor well but need help structuring it.
limits.card4Title: We don't talk to your university
limits.card4Body: Yet. Right now, students sign up directly and add Inturn internships to their CV themselves. University-side dashboards are on the roadmap for Phase 2 — not Phase 1.

whatYouGet.titleLead: A system for hiring interns the way you hire
whatYouGet.deck: Scope-first. Output-tracked. Accountable on both sides. The difference from a contractor: a 12-week ceiling, mentorship as part of the deal, and pay rates that actually work for students.
whatYouGet.card1Body: Define 3–10 deliverables before publishing. Inturn won't let you skip this. The deliverables become the workspace tabs the intern sees every day — the brief is the contract.
whatYouGet.card2Title: A workspace per intern, not per company
whatYouGet.card2Body: Each intern works in their own workspace under the project. Multi-intern projects (design + research, frontend + backend) coordinate via shared activity feed but ship independently.
whatYouGet.card3Body: Pre-scheduled. Same Jitsi link every week. Auto-generated agenda from what shipped, what's blocked, what's overdue. You show up; the system does the prep.
whatYouGet.card4Title: Reviewable in five minutes a day
whatYouGet.card4Body: The dashboard pulls every "needs review" item across all your interns into one place. Five minutes a day keeps the loop alive — and the data shows companies who do this finish projects on time at 4× the rate.
whatYouGet.card5Body: Save any finished project as a template. Next year's intern run starts from your own playbook, not a blank page. Most teams hit "5× faster than the first one" by year two.
whatYouGet.card6Body: The interns who finish strong on Inturn are the ones you hire full-time later. Every certificate links to a portfolio of real work — when you re-recruit, you know what you're getting.

supervisor.point1Body: Purple bar at top names what needs your attention, who submitted it, when. One click jumps to the card.
supervisor.point2Body: Submissions get a purple outline on the board. Impossible to scroll past — and the count badge on the tab reminds you on every workspace.
supervisor.point3Body: Orange left-border for things due this week. Red for overdue. Neutral for the rest. The product doesn't yell — it just doesn't let you forget.

quote.text: Before Inturn, I was the bottleneck. I felt guilty all the time. After Inturn, I review on the bus and the work moves while I sleep. I went from one intern a year to three.

useCases.card3Body: Copy refreshes, social campaigns, blog series, video. Brief-driven, deliverable-heavy — exactly the kind of work that benefits from the versioned-deliverable loop.

whatYouGet.titleTail: with a portfolio, not a panic.
whatYouGet.card1Body: Every listing says upfront whether it's unpaid or offers an indemnité — and exactly how much. Most internships in Tunisia are unpaid or carry a small monthly indemnité; here you always know before you apply. No "we'll discuss it later."
whatYouGet.card2Body: Every internship has deliverables defined upfront. You know what's expected from day one. No more arriving Monday and finding out there's "nothing for you to do today."
whatYouGet.card3Body: Tasks, weekly check-ins, comments, deliverables versioning — all in one place. The supervisor sees everything you ship. You see everything you've done.
whatYouGet.card4Body: The AI matches you to roles based on skills, location, goals — and is honest when the fit isn't great. A 92% match means apply; a 54% match means you can, but stretch.
whatYouGet.card5Body: Inturn flags reviews older than 48 hours on the supervisor's dashboard. You won't be left waiting two weeks for feedback. If you are, you can escalate inside the app.
whatYouGet.card6Body: At the end, your certificate is verifiable at inturn.app/v/'{your-id}' — employers can check it, see what you shipped, see your supervisor's rating. Worth more than a PDF.

meta.description: Structured async internships that actually work remotely. Intern for a team beyond your city — even beyond Tunisia — inside one workspace with task templates, weekly check-ins and verifiable deliverables.

hero.titleLead: Work with a team beyond your city.
hero.deck: A virtual internship on Inturn isn't a Zoom link and good luck. It's the same structured workspace — async task templates, weekly check-ins, versioned deliverables — built so remote actually works. And Tunis runs on Central European time, so a day with a Paris or Berlin team lines up by default.

whyFails.titleLead: Remote doesn't break on distance. It breaks on
whyFails.deck: The reason "virtual intern" sounds risky is that most remote internships are an email and a vague hope. Inturn removes the three things that actually kill them.
whyFails.card1Body: With no shared desk, feedback goes quiet. So check-ins are weekly and mandatory, and any review older than 48h gets flagged on the supervisor's dashboard. The loop can't drift.
whyFails.card2Body: Remote turns a fuzzy task into a week lost. Every task ships as an async template — scope, output, deadline — so there's nothing to "hop on a call to explain."
whyFails.card3Body: Work done remotely tends to vanish. Here every submission is versioned in Deliverables, and the internship ends with a verifiable certificate that links to exactly what shipped.

howItRuns.deck: The same workspace your on-site interns use — tuned so the default is writing things down, not booking meetings.
howItRuns.step1Title: Every task carries its own brief
howItRuns.step1Body: When a supervisor adds work, they fill scope, expected output, and a deadline — in the company's timezone, shown in yours. The intern never has to guess what "done" means, and never waits for a call to start.
howItRuns.step2Title: A five-minute rhythm that can't be skipped
howItRuns.step2Body: Each week the intern files a short check-in — shipped, blocked, next — and the supervisor is notified the moment it lands. It's the heartbeat that keeps a remote internship from going dark between deadlines.
howItRuns.step3Title: One click to a call, in both timezones
howItRuns.step3Body: When something does need a conversation, "Schedule a check-in" generates a Meet or Jitsi link and lands it on both calendars with the times already converted. We don't build video — we build the structure around it.
howItRuns.step4Title: It ends with proof, not a "thanks for your time"
howItRuns.step4Body: Every submission is versioned and reviewed in the open. At the finish line the certificate links to the deliverables, the tasks closed, and the supervisor's rating — verifiable at inturn.app/v/'{id}', wherever the work happened.

opportunity.deck: Virtual doesn't just mean "from home in Tunis." It means a student in Sfax can intern with a studio in the capital — or a startup in Paris — without moving. Tunisia sits an hour, at most, from European business hours, which makes it one of the easiest places in the world to do real async work for a European team.
opportunity.stat1Label: Central European time — at most an hour from Paris, Berlin or Madrid.
opportunity.stat2Label: commute. Your city stops being the limit on which teams you can join.

split.internsTitle: Your city stops deciding your career.
split.internsBody: The best role for you might be at a studio two governorates away, or a remote-first team abroad. Virtual internships put those on your list. Same profile, same one-click apply — and the same certificate at the end, which doesn't care where you sat while you earned it.
split.companiesTitle: Hire the right intern, not the nearest one.
split.companiesBody: Open a role to talent in Sfax, Sousse or anywhere with a connection, and the structure means you manage it in minutes a day: tasks carry their own briefs, check-ins come to you, reviews are flagged before they're late. Start hybrid, switch a role to virtual when you're ready — it's an opt-in, not a leap.
